text:
miriam: Heads-up — customer (internal ticket INC-4521) reports SSE/chat streams returning a first partial event then a stream disconnect when the request traverses our gRPC gateway -> HTTP/1.1 intermediary -> client. Happens only when client connects over HTTP/1.1; direct h2 to backend is fine.

devon: can you paste repro steps? which proxy in the middle? envoy or a custom nginx?

miriam: envoy at the edge, then an older haproxy box in front of the customer NAT. customer uses a long-polling SSE client in-browser. They see one "data:" line, then nothing until reconnect.

robin-support: got their logs — here's the server-side send pattern (from our handler):
```
write("event: message\n");
write("data: {\"text\": \"part1\"}\n\n");
flush(); // expected immediate delivery
// later write finishing tail:
write("data: {\"text\": \"part2\"}\n\n");
```
They confirmed the first flush reaches client but client never gets the rest; connection closes after a handful of seconds.

sam: can you capture curl traces from the client side? also check any header changes (transfer-encoding/content-length).

miriam: customer ran two tests for us:
1) curl using HTTP/2 directly to our edge (`--http2-prior-knowledge`) -> full streaming, both parts arrive as separate chunks.
2) curl forcing HTTP/1.1 (default) through their haproxy path -> only first chunk delivered, then connection closed. They provided tcpdump and a small envoy access log snippet.

harpreet: shared tcpdump highlights: the upstream (our backend) sends two small TLS records ~100ms apart. Envoy downstream -> haproxy seems to coalesce into a single 1450B packet with no intermediate flush at the haproxy->client TCP layer. Also noticed content-length header present on the client response in the haproxy leg: `content-length: 1450`. That smells like an intermediary converting h2 streaming semantics into a buffered h1 response and inserting content-length.

devon: that matches a header flip bug we tracked last quarter: if envoy translates h2 HEADERS+DATA into an h1 response and a downstream (haproxy) mistakenly buffers and sets content-length, then the browser will expect a fixed-length body and treat later flushed bytes oddly. But we usually set `transfer-encoding: chunked` for streaming. Do their logs show chunked?

robin-support: haproxy output shows `Content-Length: 1450` and no `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Envoy upstream logs show `:status 200` and `content-type: text/event-stream`.

sam: repro attempt from our side: I ran a small two-proxy chain (envoy -> nginx) and reproduced. nginx was configured with `proxy_buffering on;` which buffered small writes until `proxy_buffer_size` was full, then sent a Content-Length. When I set `proxy_buffering off;` and ensured `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passed through, the client saw both events.

miriam: good find. customer haproxy is an older release that has a default buffering behavior on TLS terminate. They won't upgrade quickly. Any mitigation we can do on our side?

harpreet: possible server-side mitigations: 1) coalesce fewer small writes (send a small heartbeat newline to keep connection alive but avoid extra flush boundaries) — but that doesn't fix content-length flip. 2) Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` / `Connection: keep-alive`? not reliable. 3) Use SSE comment prefix (`: `) every N bytes to keep proxies from collapsing? that's a heuristic.

devon: more deterministic: adjust our edge envoy translation to force `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` on the HTTP/1.1 downstream when we detect a streaming response and to set `x-envoy-streaming: 1` so intermediaries ideally pass through. We already have a flag `strip_content_length_on_streaming` in config but it was only enabled for internal nets. Let's enable it for this region and roll a canary.

miriam: can we do a quick canary for acme's region? If envoy strips content-length and enforces chunked, does that fix the haproxy behavior?

sam: I ran a canary in staging with the strip bit on. Reproduced haproxy case, and the downstream haproxy no longer sets content-length; it passes chunked frames and the client receives both events.

robin-support: great — next steps for support: propose a temporary workaround (enable our edge config) and walk the customer through toggling their haproxy to `option http-server-close` or disabling buffering. Also offer a targeted canary in their region.

harpreet: filing internal ticket ENG-RUNTIME-778 to make `strip_content_length_on_streaming` more robust and add an automatic detector when `content-type: text/event-stream` + `grpc-gateway` trickery. I'll attach tcpdumps and nginx repro.

devon: also logging note — add an observability flag to surface when we detect a downstream `Content-Length` on a streaming response (sample 1 per minute), so we can catch other customers behind the same type of proxy.

miriam: assigned to eng-runtime and support to coordinate the customer canary. Robin will own customer comms. @robin-support can you draft the response (workaround + ETA)?

robin-support: on it. Suggested message: "We're seeing a downstream intermediary convert the streaming response into a fixed-length response. We can enable a safe edge configuration to force chunked transfer on streaming endpoints immediately; if you'd prefer we can also walk you through a temporary haproxy setting change. Either option should restore continuous SSE events while we push a permanent fix." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Deploy request created: deploy/edge/strip-content-length-canary -> canary-2345 (deployer: devon).

miriam: thanks all — keep thread updated with canary results and customer's reply.

sam: quick reminder commands we used to repro:
```bash
# direct h2 (works):
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -v "https://edge.redwood.example/sse-chat?user=acme"
# force http1.1 via haproxy path (fails):
curl -v "https://edge.redwood.example/sse-chat?user=acme" --http1.1
# tcpdump filter for the middlebox leg:
tcpdump -i eth0 -w haproxy-leg.pcap host 10.1.2.3 and port 443
```

miriam: perfect — saving logs to INC-4521 and ENG-RUNTIME-778. Closing loop once canary confirms. :white_check_mark:
